correctness.rationale: The first three branches follow directly from set inclusion and uniqueness of single-ball projection. If neither single-ball projection is feasible, convex projection optimality excludes zero or one active constraint, so both sphere boundaries are active. The common boundary is a sphere in the radical hyperplane with the displayed center and radius, and orthogonal decomposition reduces nearest-point projection onto that sphere to a Cauchy--Schwarz equality. Nonempty interior excludes external tangency, while containment and concentric cases are already caught by a single-ball branch. Uniqueness of projection onto the convex lens excludes the degenerate \(w=0\) case when the seam radius is positive.

originality.rationale: The recent optimization source explicitly requires exact two-ball projections and states that the simultaneous-active case is handled through a two-dimensional dual system or Dykstra iteration. The closest exact geometric prior gives projection onto the intersection of two sphere boundaries, not the complete convex lens projector. An earlier optimization application likewise uses Dykstra for an intersection of two closed balls. Targeted searches over ball-lens, KKT, nearest-point, radical-hyperplane, and closed-form aliases found no published statement equivalent to the complete active-set formula.

value.rationale: The exact two-ball projection is load-bearing in the recent certified-localization algorithm: every accelerated inner step uses it to remain inside a region where ordinary smoothness is certified, and the source explicitly separates its cost from gradient complexity. Replacing an iterative dual or Dykstra subsolve by a finite \(O(n)\) formula makes this oracle constructive at the same ambient order as a single ball projection. This is a concrete algorithmic simplification of a repeatedly invoked primitive, not an arbitrary geometric exercise. The limitation to exact-real arithmetic is stated, so the result does not overclaim a finite-precision robustness guarantee.
